contexts.text: The man of the Church called Noah... who is described by the ark. AC 639. AC 655. AC 896.
The formation (of the new Church, called Noah) is described by the ark, into which were received all the living creatures. AC 811.
The Flood, ark, and the things described in relation to them, signify regeneration, and also the temptations that precede it.
By the ark... are signified arcana... In like manner by the little ark in which Moses was hidden... and still more loftily by the holy ark in the wilderness...

This first description of the ark, that it was constructed of Gopher wood, (with) stories, and was bituminated with bitumen outside and inside, involves that the other part, that of the will, was preserved from inundation, and only that part was opened which is of the understanding, and which is described by the window, the door, the lowest, the second, and the third.
The numbers, or measures, of the ark, signify... the remains that were with the man of this Church, while he was being reformed, and that they were few.
He entered into the ark... = that he was saved. AC 764.
Enter thou, and all thy house into the ark = those things which are of the will.
To enter into the ark is to be prepared.

As to its being here said that unclean beasts were also to be introduced into the ark, the case stands thus; there is here described the man of this Church, what sort of a man he was, and that in fact by the ark, and thus by the things that were in the ark, or that were introduced into the ark; that is, which were with the man before he was regenerated...
Noah entered into the ark from before the waters of the Flood = that he was safe. AC 748.
They entered into the ark = that they were saved. AC 779.

The fluctuations of the man of this Church are described... also by the waters, that is, falsities, bearing up the ark; further, that it was elevated above the earth... at last, that the ark went upon the faces of the waters. Explained.

So long as he remained in the ark, he was in a state of servitude, or of captivity, or imprisonment; being tossed about by the waters of the Flood... His state of freedom is described, not only by Noah's going forth from the ark, but also all things that were with him. AC 905. AC 912. AC 918.
All that go forth from the ark = the men of the Church... or the regenerate. AC 1061.
Till the day that Noah entered into the ark = the end of the former Church, and the beginning of the new one. The ark = the Church itself.
